Bug_Details: @CanIgnoreReturnValue should not be applied to classes as it almost always overmatches (as it applies to constructors and all methods), and the CIRVness isn't conferred to its subclasses.
Bug_Explanation: @CanIgnoreReturnValue should not be applied to classes as it applies to all methods and constructors within the class, leading to overmatching. This does not make sense semantically since not all methods within a class should necessarily have their return values ignored. The annotation should be used on specific methods instead.
Trigger_Explanation: The testShowBug() method in the JUnit test class RandomNumberGeneratorTest calls the showBug() method, which uses RandomNumberGenerator's method with a @CanIgnoreReturnValue annotation incorrectly applied to the class. This causes the test to fail because the assertion expects an incorrect value, demonstrating that the return value should not be ignored.
